lesson.title: 2D Shapes, Angles and Symmetry: Describe and Classify Shapes
lesson.explanation: Two-dimensional (2D) shapes are flat shapes. Describe them by their sides, corners (vertices), straight or curved edges, and special properties. A triangle has three sides; a quadrilateral has four. A rectangle has four right angles, and a square has four equal sides as well as four right angles. An angle measures a turn: a right angle is 90°, an acute angle is smaller than 90°, and an obtuse angle is greater than 90° but less than 180°. A line of symmetry splits a shape into two matching mirror halves.

examples.problem: A shape has four straight sides and four right angles. What shape could it be?

steps.result: There are four straight sides, so it is a quadrilateral.
All four angles are right angles.

steps.instruction: Use the properties to name possible shapes.
steps.result: It could be a rectangle; if all sides are equal too, it is a square.

examples.answer: A rectangle; it is a square too if all four sides are equal.
examples.visual_description: Show a rectangle and a square, highlighting their right angles and side lengths.

steps.instruction: Recall the size of a right angle.

examples.visual_description: Draw one 45-degree angle beside a square-corner right-angle marker.

examples.problem: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?

steps.instruction: Imagine folding the triangle through a line from one vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.
Try the same fold from each of the other two vertices.
steps.result: Each fold also makes matching halves.

examples.answer: An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry.
examples.visual_description: Draw the three symmetry lines from each vertex to the opposite side midpoint.

practice_problems.question: How many sides does a pentagon have?
practice_problems.explanation: The prefix penta- means five; a pentagon has five sides.

practice_problems.question: What type of angle is exactly 90°?
hints: Think of the corner of a square.
practice_problems.explanation: A 90-degree angle is a right angle.

practice_problems.question: Is a 45° angle acute or obtuse?
practice_problems.explanation: 45° is less than 90°, so it is acute.

practice_problems.question: A rectangle has a length of 5 cm and width of 3 cm. How many right angles does it have?
hints: Count the corners of the rectangle.
practice_problems.explanation: Every rectangle has four right angles.

practice_problems.question: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
practice_problems.explanation: A fold through each vertex and the opposite side midpoint splits it into matching halves.

practice_problems.question: A shape has 4 equal sides but no right angles. Could it be a square?
practice_problems.answer: No. A square must have four equal sides and four right angles.
hints: Check both the sides and the angles.
practice_problems.explanation: Equal side lengths alone are not enough; angle properties also matter.
distractors: Yes, any shape with four sides is a square.
A square has exactly three right angles.
Only if it has five sides.

practice_problems.question: Draw or describe a quadrilateral that is not a rectangle and explain one property.
practice_problems.answer: Answers vary; for example, a parallelogram has two pairs of opposite sides parallel and need not have right angles.
hints: Choose a four-sided shape with a different angle or side property.
practice_problems.explanation: A valid example must have four sides and a property that distinguishes it from a rectangle.
distractors: A triangle with three sides and two pairs of parallel sides is a quadrilateral.
It must have exactly three sides.

hints: Count straight sides and vertices; do not confuse a side with a corner.
Compare angles with a right angle of 90°.
A line of symmetry makes two matching mirror halves.

key_vocabulary.definition: A corner where two sides meet.
A 2D shape with four straight sides.
A property where two parts match across a line or around a point.
key_vocabulary.example_usage: A square has four lines of symmetry.

misconceptions.misconception: Every four-sided shape is a rectangle.
misconceptions.correction: A rectangle also needs four right angles.
misconceptions.why_students_think_this: Side count alone does not define a shape's angle properties.

misconceptions.misconception: A line drawn through a shape is always a line of symmetry.
misconceptions.correction: Both sides must match as mirror images across that line.
misconceptions.why_students_think_this: Symmetry is a property of matching halves, not simply a line on the page.

assessment.title: Assessment: 2D Shapes, Angles and Symmetry: Describe and Classify Shapes

items.question: How many sides does a quadrilateral have?
What is one property shared by a square and a rectangle?
Why is a square a special rectangle?
items.correct_answer: It has four right angles like every rectangle, and all four of its sides are equal.
items.hint: Compare both angle and side properties.

items.question: A learner calls a 120° angle acute. Is the classification correct?
items.correct_answer: No. 120° is greater than 90° and less than 180°, so it is obtuse.

items.question: Describe how you would test whether a paper shape has a line of symmetry.
items.correct_answer: Fold it along the proposed line; the two halves should match exactly.
items.hint: Imagine or make a fold along the line.
